conceptTag: Write a value proposition for a local gym
readerTitle: Every gym says "friendly staff." Write the line only yours can say.
caseNote: 가상 사례 (동네 헬스장, 동네 철물점, 대기업 사내 데이터팀) · 적용 레슨으로 새 개념 없이 가치 제안과 고객의 차선책을 사용
insight: 가치 제안은 내 가게의 장점 목록이 아니라, 특정 고객이 지금 쓰고 있는 차선책과 비교한 한 문장이다.
misconception: 가치 제안은 우리 시설과 서비스의 좋은 점을 최대한 많이 나열하는 것이고, 비교 대상은 길 건너 경쟁사다.

sources.text: 단원 개념 레슨 CUS-02-03(가치 제안), CUS-02-05(고객의 차선책)를 적용
모든 사례와 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 헬스장, 철물점, 사내 데이터팀은 모두 가상 사례입니다. 회원 인터뷰 20명, 운영 시간, 수업 시간 등 모든 수치는 설명용이며 실제 통계가 아닙니다.
가치 제안 문장 틀(For… who… we… unlike…)은 널리 쓰이는 일반적 형식으로 소개했으며 특정 저자의 프레임워크 이름은 쓰지 않았습니다. CUS-02-03 본문의 표현과 일치하는지 확인하세요.

cards.title: Every gym on the street says the same thing.
body: Dana runs a small gym. Her sign reads: *Modern equipment. Friendly staff. Real results.*
The budget chain two blocks away says almost the same. So does the studio across the road. A passer-by can't tell the three apart. Dana wants to rewrite her sign and website this week.

image.label: Three gym signs with nearly identical slogans
image.brief: 동네 거리에 헬스장 간판 세 개가 나란히 걸려 있고, 모두 "Modern equipment", "Friendly staff" 같은 비슷한 문구. 행인 한 명이 고개를 갸웃. 실제 브랜드 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Who should Dana compare herself against?
body: Before choosing words, Dana needs a comparison. Her message will say "better than ___." Which blank should drive it?

options.text: The budget chain two blocks away
options.feedback: It's the obvious rival, but it may not be what her members chose against. Leading with it pulls her into a price fight she can't win.

options.text: Whatever her members did before they joined
options.feedback: This is the **next best alternative**: what the customer would actually do without you. It's often not a competitor at all.

options.text: The premium studio across the road
options.feedback: Aiming upward sounds ambitious, but if few members ever considered the studio, the message answers a question nobody asked.

cards.title: The real rival was a membership nobody used.
body: Dana asked 20 recent members why they joined. Most were working parents in their 30s and 40s.
Their story repeated: they had joined a big gym before, felt lost on the floor, missed the 6 p.m. slot because of school pickup, and quietly stopped going while still paying.
So the alternative wasn't another gym. It was **paying for a gym and not going**, or not exercising at all.

cards.title: Fill in four blanks.
body: A **value proposition** says who it's for, the problem it solves, what you offer, and why that beats their alternative. Dana's first pass:
list: **Who:** keep quitting gyms they pay for
**We offer:** 45-minute coached sessions at 6 a.m. and 8 p.m.
**Unlike:** a big gym where nobody notices you stop coming

image.label: Four fill-in-the-blank boxes forming one sentence
image.brief: 빈칸 네 개(For / Who / We offer / Unlike)가 화살표로 이어져 한 문장이 되는 인포그래픽. 각 빈칸에 위 리스트 문구를 손글씨 느낌으로 채움.

cards.title: Which line goes on the sign?
body: Dana has room for one headline. Which one should she use?

options.text: Classes for every fitness level, morning to night
options.feedback: True and welcoming, but every gym can say it. It describes the gym, not the **value proposition** for a specific customer.

options.text: Busy parent? 45-minute coached sessions at 6 and 8, and a coach who checks in when you miss one
options.feedback: It names the customer and answers their real alternative: quitting unnoticed. You give up broad appeal to be unmistakable to the people who matter most.
Bold, but it competes on a promise she can't control, and it ignores why her members actually left other gyms.

cards.title: A value proposition is a promise.
body: If the coach doesn't actually check in, the sign becomes a liability. Write only what operations can deliver every week.

A narrow line also means some people won't feel addressed. That's the cost of being clear. Test it with behavior, such as how many people book a trial, rather than asking friends if they like the wording.

cards.title: A hardware store finds its real rival.
body: A neighborhood hardware store assumed its rival was the big-box store. Talking to contractors, the owner learned their alternative was *driving 20 minutes at 7 a.m. and losing an hour of billable work*.
New line: "For local contractors: open at 6, text your list the night before, and your parts are waiting at the counter."
cards.softwareNote: For many software tools, the next best alternative is a spreadsheet or email thread. A proposition that says "unlike rebuilding the sheet every Monday" usually lands harder than one comparing features with a rival app.

cards.title: Now it's a team inside a large company.
body: You lead the in-house analytics team at a large distributor. Few departments use you. Sales managers say they build their own pipeline reports in spreadsheets every Monday.
Which pitch should you send them?

options.text: We're the official analytics team, with enterprise-grade tools
options.feedback: It talks about you, not them. Managers don't need better tools; they need their Monday morning back.

options.text: Ask us for a report on any metric, any time
options.feedback: Flexible, but it adds a request step their spreadsheet doesn't have. Against that **next best alternative**, it can feel like more work.

options.text: For sales managers who rebuild Monday reports: your pipeline report in your inbox by 8 a.m., no exports
options.feedback: It names who, the pain and why it beats the spreadsheet. That's a complete **value proposition** aimed at the real alternative.

cards.title: Write against what customers actually do instead.
body: Concepts used: **the value proposition** (who, problem, offer, why better) and **the customer's next best alternative** (the real comparison, often not a competitor).
**Try it today:** ask three recent customers what they did before they found you. Rewrite your headline so it beats that.
